fractional-advisory-day.name: Fractional Advisory Day
fractional-advisory-day.who: Leadership teams who need to know where to look first
fractional-advisory-day.next: Automation Starter, or the Diagnostic Assessment
fractional-advisory-day.blurb: A working session with your leadership team, structured around where the business loses time and money rather than around what AI can do.
fractional-advisory-day.sum: A working session with your leadership team, structured around where the business loses time and money rather than around what AI can do. You have the written summary the following morning.
items: A working session with your leadership team
Half a day on site, built around your operations rather than a generic agenda.
A live opportunity map
Every candidate use case surfaced in the session, captured and sorted by value and feasibility while the team watches it happen.
A same day written summary
Delivered within twenty four hours, not two weeks. Three to five pages, no filler.
A go and no go list
The opportunities worth pursuing, and the ones that will waste money, with the reason stated for each.
A governance flag list
Anything currently exposing the business, identified and named.
One immediate action
The single move to make this week, with the owner named.
fractional-advisory-day.then: Most clients leave the day with one opportunity they want proved. That is the Automation Starter. If the picture is broader than one process, the Diagnostic Assessment is the right next step.

ai-foundations-day.name: AI Foundations Day
ai-foundations-day.req: Follows the AI Readiness Score or a diagnostic finding
ai-foundations-day.who: Teams already using AI without agreed ground rules
ai-foundations-day.next: Shadow AI Audit, or the Diagnostic Assessment
ai-foundations-day.blurb: The full day version. Direction in the morning, working practice in the afternoon, for teams that would rather do it in one visit.
ai-foundations-day.sum: A full day for up to fifteen people. The morning covers risk and reward and the ground rules. The afternoon is hands on, working on their own real tasks. Nobody leaves with a handout they will never open again.
items: A pre-session readiness read
Attendees complete the free AI Readiness Score first, so the day is shaped by this business rather than a generic curriculum.
A full day on site for up to fifteen people
Morning on risk and reward. Afternoon on doing the work. No slides after lunch.
A one page set of ground rules
The dos and the do nots, written in your language, ready to put on the wall or in the handbook.
A red lines list
What must never be entered into a public AI tool, named specifically for your data and your client obligations.
A prompt library built from your own tasks
Fifteen to twenty working prompts your team writes in the room, on their real work, tested before they leave.
A named internal owner and a thirty day practice plan
Who keeps this alive, what they do weekly, and how you will know it is working.
One immediate action
The single change to make on Monday morning.
ai-foundations-day.then: A team that has just written its own red lines list usually asks what else is exposed. That question is answered by the Shadow AI Audit or, if it runs deeper, the Diagnostic Assessment.

automation-starter.name: Automation Starter
automation-starter.who: Businesses that want proof rather than paper
automation-starter.blurb: One process, scoped with your team, built in the systems you already pay for, measured before and after, and handed over.
automation-starter.sum: Every other engagement at this price produces a document. This one produces a working thing. One process, scoped with your team, built in the systems you already pay for, measured before and after, and handed over.
items: A scoped process
One workflow chosen with the team, with the time it currently takes and the errors it currently produces written down before anything is built.
A working automation
Built in the tools the business already pays for, running on live work, with the exception paths handled rather than ignored.
A before and after measure
Hours, handoffs and errors counted at the start and again at handover, so the return is a number rather than a claim.
A handover pack and a named owner
How it works, how to change it, how to switch it off, and the person inside the business who runs it without us.
The next two candidates, ranked
The following processes worth automating, in order, with the reason each one is next.
automation-starter.then: Once one process is running and measured, the next two are already ranked. The Automation Sprint takes on two or three connected processes with the controls to run them safely.

shadow-ai-audit.name: Shadow AI Audit
shadow-ai-audit.who: Any business where staff are already using AI unsupervised
shadow-ai-audit.blurb: Which people are using which AI tools, on what work, with what data, and what to do about it.
shadow-ai-audit.sum: Most businesses of sixty to a hundred and fifty people have staff putting client information into consumer AI tools right now. This establishes which people, which tools, which data, and what to do about it.
items: A full picture of current AI use
Which tools, which teams, on what work. Gathered by structured staff survey and systems review.
A data exposure assessment
What information is leaving the business, and where that creates client, contractual or regulatory risk.
A licence and spend reconciliation
What is paid for, what is used, and the gap in both directions.
A risk register
Every exposure rated, with a named owner and a mitigation.
A remediation sequence
What to stop this week, what to control this month, and what to formalise this quarter.
shadow-ai-audit.then: The audit tells you what is exposed. If the underlying issue is that nobody agreed the rules, the Foundations Day fixes it. If it runs broader than governance, the Diagnostic Assessment is the next step.

ai-starting-point.name: AI Starting Point
ai-starting-point.who: Owners and leadership deciding where AI belongs
ai-starting-point.next: AI in Practice, or Automation Starter
ai-starting-point.blurb: A half day that answers where AI belongs in this business, and just as usefully, where it does not.
ai-starting-point.sum: For a business still working out whether any of this applies to them. Half a day with the people who decide, ending in a shortlist of three opportunities with a rough return against each, rather than a list of tools to go and look at.
items: A short pre-session read
Your AI Readiness Score reviewed before we arrive, so the session starts from your position rather than from first principles.
A half day working session
With the owner and whoever else makes the call, built around where the business loses time and money.
A shortlist of the three strongest opportunities
Named specifically, in your operation, not drawn from a sector case study.
A rough return against each
What it is plausibly worth in a year, and what it depends on being true.
A basic safety checklist
What to put in place before anyone starts, sized to a business of your kind.
One immediate action
The single move to make this week, with the owner named.
ai-starting-point.then: Knowing where AI belongs is not the same as your people knowing how to use it. AI in Practice is the follow through, and it is £995 when booked within thirty days of this session.

ai-in-practice.name: AI in Practice
ai-in-practice.bundle: £995 when booked within thirty days of an AI Starting Point session
ai-in-practice.dur: Half a day on site, up to twelve people
ai-in-practice.blurb: Half a day with a working team, on their own tasks, in their own tools. Everyone leaves with at least one thing that works on Monday.
ai-in-practice.sum: A working session for the people who do the work, not the people who decide. Their laptops, their real tasks, their actual tools. Generic examples are what makes this kind of session forgettable, so the material comes from the team itself.
items: Pre-work built from real tasks
Each attendee submits two things from their actual week that they suspect could be faster. Those become the material.
What these tools are and are not
Twenty minutes in plain terms, and no theory beyond that.
Safe use, covered first
What must never be pasted into a public tool, what counts as client data, and who to ask. Early in the session, not as a closing caveat.
Working patterns by role
Three or four role groups, each building against the tasks they submitted.
A live build
Everyone leaves with at least one working thing they can use immediately.
Where it stops
The limits named out loud, so nobody later trusts an output they should not have.
A working patterns library within five working days
Specific to their roles, with a one page acceptable use summary and a named internal point of contact agreed in the room.
ai-in-practice.then: A team using AI well on its own tasks starts noticing the processes that should not need a person at all. That is the Automation Starter.

automation-sprint.name: Automation Sprint
automation-sprint.who: Businesses ready to move beyond one proven process
automation-sprint.blurb: Two or three connected processes mapped, automated, measured and handed over, with the controls needed to run them safely.
automation-sprint.sum: Two or three connected processes mapped, automated, measured and handed over, with the controls needed to run them safely. A deck is a promise. A running process is a receipt.
items: A process map of the target area
Two or three connected workflows mapped end to end, with the time and cost of every step recorded.
Two to three automations built and running
In your own systems, on live work, with exception handling and a fallback for when the tool is wrong.
A measured baseline and result
Hours, handoffs and error rates before and after, so the payback is evidence rather than an estimate.
A control and governance wrapper
Who can change what, what is logged, and what a human must still sign before it goes out.
A handover pack and a named internal owner
Documentation, an escalation route, and a person inside the business who can run it after we leave.
The next wave, ranked
What to automate next, in order, with the dependency each one carries.
One immediate action
The single move to make before the next process is touched.
automation-sprint.then: A business with three processes running and a measured return needs a plan for the rest of them. That is the Strategy & Roadmap.

data-readiness-check.name: Data Readiness Check
data-readiness-check.who: Businesses about to invest in AI that depends on their own data
data-readiness-check.blurb: Most AI programmes fail on data rather than on models. This establishes what your data can actually support before you spend.
data-readiness-check.sum: Most AI programmes fail on data rather than on models. This establishes what your data can actually support before you spend money finding out the hard way.
items: A data inventory
What the business holds, where it sits, and what condition it is in.
A quality and completeness assessment
Scored per system, with the specific gaps that would break a use case named.
An integration read
What connects to what today, and what would need to be built.
A permissions and lawful basis review
What the business is permitted to use, and for what purpose.
A readiness verdict per use case
Which use cases your current data can support, which need work first, and how much work.
data-readiness-check.then: Sometimes the honest answer is that the business is not ready yet, and we will say so. Where the data holds up, the Diagnostic Assessment turns it into a prioritised plan.

diagnostic-assessment.name: Diagnostic Assessment
diagnostic-assessment.who: Businesses committing real budget and needing evidence first
diagnostic-assessment.blurb: Evidence based, not self reported. The foundation everything after it is built on.
diagnostic-assessment.sum: We gather the evidence ourselves rather than taking a self assessment at face value. Interviews, a systems review and a working session on site, assessed against the same underlying framework, so nothing is wasted moving to the next stage.
items: Findings gathered first hand
Interviews, a systems review and a working session, rather than a questionnaire filled in by one person.
Results broken down by function, team and process
Not one blended score, because the blended picture almost always hides where the problem actually sits.
The single constraint holding the business back most
Named plainly, with what it costs you annually.
Three prioritised opportunities, costed
Each with an outline of what it depends on before it can work.
One immediate action
The single move worth making before the roadmap is written.
diagnostic-assessment.then: The Diagnostic establishes what is true. The Strategy & Roadmap turns it into a plan the leadership team can run. They are priced and bought separately, so you can stop here if the evidence says you should.

strategy-roadmap.name: Strategy & Roadmap
strategy-roadmap.who: Businesses with the evidence, needing the plan
strategy-roadmap.blurb: Turns the diagnostic into a plan the leadership team can actually run.
strategy-roadmap.sum: The findings turned into a phased twelve month plan with owners, decision points, a governance position sized to the business, and an agreed way to tell whether it is working.
items: A phased roadmap covering the next twelve months
What happens when, in what order, with named owners and decision points between phases.
Prioritisation based on your real KPIs
Use cases ranked against the measures the business already runs on, not against a generic scoring model.
A business case per use case
Cost, value at stake and payback, so each one can be approved or declined on its own merits.
A governance position sized to the business
Proportionate controls. What needs signing, what needs logging, and what does not need either.
A way to measure whether the plan is working
Agreed before it starts, measured against the baseline from the Diagnostic.
strategy-roadmap.then: From here the work is delivery. We build the first priority use case, or your team does with our support. Either way the roadmap is yours to keep.

pilot-delivery-sprint.name: Pilot Delivery Sprint
pilot-delivery-sprint.who: Clients with a roadmap and a first use case to build
pilot-delivery-sprint.blurb: Where the roadmap gets built, not just written. The first priority use case, running on live work.
pilot-delivery-sprint.sum: A fixed scope build of the first priority use case from your roadmap, with a defined success measure agreed at the outset and a checkpoint partway through, so spend stays controlled.
items: The first priority use case built and running
Scoped and priced before anything starts, then built in your own systems on live work.
A defined success measure
Agreed at the outset, so nobody argues afterwards about whether it worked.
A clear checkpoint partway through
A genuine stop point, so spend stays controlled. If the evidence does not support continuing, we say so.
A full handover once the use case is proven
Documentation, an escalation route, and people inside the business who can run it without us.
pilot-delivery-sprint.then: Delivered work needs to keep working. The Continuing Partnership keeps the governance current and re scores you against your original baseline.

ai-champions-programme.name: AI Champions Programme
ai-champions-programme.who: Businesses whose capability must survive after we leave
ai-champions-programme.blurb: An internal cohort equipped and supported so the capability stays inside the business. Sequenced after the roadmap, never before it.
ai-champions-programme.sum: An internal cohort equipped and supported so the capability stays inside the business. Sequenced after the roadmap, never before it, so the cohort works on real priorities rather than hypotheticals.
items: A selected internal cohort
Chosen with you, on the basis of who actually influences how work gets done.
A working programme built on your roadmap
The cohort works on the priorities already agreed, not on generic exercises.
Supported practice over ten to twelve weeks
Regular sessions with real work in between, rather than a single day that fades.
A shared internal playbook
Written by the cohort, owned by the business, and kept current after we leave.
A capability handover
Named owners, an escalation route, and a plan for bringing on the next cohort without us.
ai-champions-programme.then: Once capability sits inside the business, the Continuing Partnership keeps it current as tools, regulation and priorities change.

continuing-partnership.name: Continuing Partnership
continuing-partnership.who: Clients past the roadmap who need the work to keep working
continuing-partnership.blurb: Ongoing, shaped around the business rather than a fixed package.
continuing-partnership.sum: A steady cadence of strategy and governance check ins, direct access as new questions and tools come up, and a periodic re score against your original baseline so progress stays visible.
items: A steady cadence of strategy and governance check ins
Regular sessions on what has moved, what has stalled, and what to reprioritise.
Direct access to the team
Not an account manager. The people who did the work, available as new questions or tools come up.
A periodic re score against the original baseline
The same instrument, re run, so progress is measured rather than claimed.
Ongoing enablement to keep capability current
Your people supported as tools, regulation and priorities change.
A quarterly business review and executive update
Written for the board, not for us.
continuing-partnership.then: Reviewed every quarter. If the value is not there, you stop. We would rather you left than stayed out of habit.
